subject: BrightPath hosted API: data residency, retention & deletion clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Simmons <claire.simmons@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API - Data residency & retention questions

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this. BrightPath's security review has a couple of focused items around data residency, retention, and deletion for the hosted API. Can you confirm the behavior for the following so we can close these questions in our questionnaire? Short bullets preferred.

1) Where are request/response payloads stored (region and services) for the hosted API? Are there any auxiliary systems that may route data to a different region?
2) Default retention windows for: (a) raw request/response logs, (b) KV/prefix caches, (c) embeddings/derived artifacts, (d) aggregated telemetry used for billing.
3) What is the deletion process and timeline when a customer requests data erasure? How long until data is irrecoverable on primary storage and backups?
4) Can you provide evidence/artifacts we can use in our audit (sample deletion log, playbook, region map)?
5) Legal hold / compliance exceptions — how are holds enforced and how do they affect deletion timelines?

Appreciate concise answers and any attachments. If you'd prefer a short call, we can schedule one.

Best,
Claire
Security Manager, BrightPath Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Simmons <claire.simmons@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - Data residency & retention questions

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Answering concisely below and attaching a few artifacts (see PDF + sample log). If anything needs more detail we can follow up or hop on a 20-minute call.

1) Residency (where data is stored):
- Primary: Customer-chosen region (US, EU, APAC) for request/response and customer data when region pinning is selected.
- Auxiliary services: Some operational telemetry (health metrics and crash dumps) and third-party monitoring traces may be routed to Redwood's US telemetry tier unless you opt into regionally isolated telemetry (enterprise option).
- Attach: hosted-data-residency-map.pdf (diagram of region boundaries + auxiliary service locations).

2) Default retention windows (out of the box):
- Raw request/response logs: 30 days by default. Enterprise plans can select 0 days (no retention) or longer up to 365 days via contractual addendum.
- KV/prefix caches: short-lived cache; default TTL is 24 hours for KV cache entries and 2 hours for in-memory prefix caching. Caches are not considered a primary store for customer data.
- Embeddings / derived artifacts: configurable; default 90 days. Customers can opt to disable storing embeddings entirely.
- Aggregated telemetry / billing metrics: retained 13 months for invoicing and usage analytics. Individual payloads are not retained in that aggregated store.

3) Deletion process & timeline on customer erasure requests:
- Step 1 (logical deletion): Within 24 hours we mark the data as deleted in the metadata index and prevent further access.
- Step 2 (primary storage purge): Primary indexes and object store purge follows within 30 days (default retention window for request/response).
- Step 3 (cache eviction): KV and in-memory caches are evicted immediately; full eviction within 48 hours for distributed caches.
- Step 4 (backups & snapshots): Backups are retained per backup lifecycle; standard snapshot retention is 90 days. Physical removal from backups occurs during normal backup retention truncation; in most cases final removal may take up to 90 days.
- Exceptions: Legal holds or ongoing investigations can pause purge operations; see (5) below.

4) Evidence/artifacts for audit:
- We can provide: deletion-playbook-v1.2.pdf (procedural steps and controls) and s3-deletion-sample-log.txt (redacted sample showing deletion event ids and timestamps). Attached.
- Formal attestation: we also provide a signed deletion attestation on request (2 business days to prepare).

5) Legal hold / compliance exceptions:
- Holds: When a customer places a legal hold, retention/erasure is suspended for the scoped data. Holds are enforced by metadata flags that prevent automatic purge jobs from removing the data.
- Escalation: Hold requests are routed to Redwood Compliance and require documented justification; holds are timeboxed and logged.
- Impact: While on hold, data remains logically accessible to support/authorized personnel per policy and will not be included in erasure runs until the hold is lifted.

Next steps: I attached the region map and deletion playbook; sample deletion log is attached. If BrightPath needs region-isolated telemetry or zero-retention hosted logs, we can add that to the contract (Aditya can scope pricing).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0176

Monica — thanks, that helps. A couple quick clarifications before we close the ticket:

• You mention primary purge within 30 days as the default. If we request immediate erasure (contractual), can Redwood accelerate primary purge to within 48 hours?
• For backups: are there any encrypted, immutable snapshots that could survive beyond the 90 day window you referenced? We need to confirm there aren’t archival tiers that hold data for longer.
• On the attestation: can you include the deletion event id and the audit log entry that shows the metadata flag change? That’s what our audit team expects.

Thanks — if easier, happy to accept the documents and then have a short call if there are policy exceptions.

Subject: Re: Hosted API - Data residency & retention questions

Hi Claire — quick answers to your follow-ups and commitments for artifacts:

• Accelerated primary purge: Yes, we can offer an accelerated purge SLA as a contractual option. Operationally we can perform a targeted primary-store purge within 48 hours for scoped data when the customer purchases the accelerated-erasure add-on. Standard (non-accelerated) erasures follow the 30-day purge window described earlier.

• Backups and immutable snapshots: By default Redwood's standard backup retention is 90 days and backups are encrypted. We do not place customer data into a long-term archival immutable cold tier unless explicitly requested and contracted. If BrightPath requires guarantees that no archival tier is used, we will add a contractual clause restricting archival exports.

• Attestation / audit artifact contents: We will provide a deletion attestation that includes: deletion event id(s), timestamps for logical deletion and physical purge job submission, and the audit log entry showing the metadata flag transition. Sample log (redacted) attached: s3-deletion-sample-log.txt. Formal attestation can be signed and returned within 2 business days.

• Additional notes on scope & guarantees:
- Legal holds: If a hold is placed, accelerated purge requests are deferred until the hold is lifted. We log all hold operations and provide the log entries in the attestation.
- Residency: We support region pinning for both primary stores and for the optional telemetry/monitoring tier; some third-party integrations (e.g., vendor-managed webhook receivers) may cross regions — we document those in the residency map.

Deliverables (today): hosted-data-residency-map.pdf, deletion-playbook-v1.2.pdf, s3-deletion-sample-log.txt (attached).
Deliverable (on request): signed deletion attestation including event IDs and audit log entries — 2 business days.

If BrightPath confirms the accelerated purge requirement, Aditya will follow up with a brief quote and contract language. Rishi, tagging you for any compliance escalation or to add SOC2 reference statements.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
